title: Sentinel Solutions - Cost economics intake
summary: Initial intake to understand token economics, hosting mix (hosted vs dedicated vs private), latency targets and security constraints. Customer wants to validate cost per user/session under 8ms P50 for short chat queries and explore batching/caching levers for a pilot. SOC2, SSO, and KMS are mandatory for production. Action items assigned for benchmark plan and security docs.
topics: dedicated GPU vs hosted fallback patterns
security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, data residency
action_items: Omar (Redwood SE): prepare a 2-day perf benchmark plan (include latency P50/P95 and token burn) - due 2028-06-09
Maya (AE): share pricing sheet and a sample pilot SOW draft - due 2028-06-05
Maya: send SOC2 report link and KMS/HSM integration notes - due 2028-06-04
Priya: provide 2 representative prompt templates and average token lengths for chat (estimates) - due 2028-06-06
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour pilot kickoff (benchmarks) with Sentinel infra - target week of 2028-06-12
Redwood to run on-hosted then dedicated instances for apples-to-apples comparison
Customer to confirm traffic mix (100k qps simulated plan) and any PII scrubbing requirements
Agree on go/no-go criteria: cost per 1k tokens, P95 latency under 120ms, and data residency compliance
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of ML, Sentinel), Connor (Platform Eng), Aisha (CISO), Samir (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Initial cost/discovery; some noisy audio on Connor at start

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros? we're Maya and Omar from Redwood.
[00:08] Priya: Hi — Priya here, Head of ML at Sentinel. We're looking into how to serve a lightweight chat assistant alongside our main product. Main questions are: how much will this burn and can we keep latencies low.
[00:20] Connor: Yeah, from infra side we care about burst patterns, and whether to use hosted for initial launch or go straight to dedicated.
[00:26] Aisha: And security — SOC2 is non-negotiable, plus SSO, SAML and KMS integration. We also have EU data residency needs.
[00:35] Omar (Redwood SE): Great, that helps. quick clarifying q — priya, what's a typical prompt/response size? tokens?
[00:41] Priya: average inbound ~ 30 tokens, outbound ~ 120 tokens for the assistant. but there's variance; some long context when the user pulls history, so maybe up to 800 tokens in worst case.
[00:53] Samir: Our VIP users might do threaded contexts; we expect 3–4 requests per session, and peak concurrent sessions around 2k for early launch.
[01:02] Maya: ok that's useful. high level, there are three paths: hosted (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput), or private/VPC (on-prem or customer VPC). each has different unit economics and tradeoffs.
[01:15] Priya: Can you give us a ballpark per-token cost difference? like hosted vs dedicated?
[01:19] Omar: ballpark numbers — hosted per-token (for our curated open models) is typically X cents per 1k tokens (note: numbers blurred in call), dedicated shifts the math: higher fixed monthly commitment but lower marginal per-token compute — maybe 30-60% cheaper at scale depending on batch efficiency. exact depends on quantization and batching.
[01:35] Connor: Batch efficiency — how sensitive is that to latency? we can't bump p50 more than 8–10ms for quick queries.
[01:42] Omar: so there's a tradeoff. continuous batching and async queues can drive down cost per token a lot, but if you enforce strict p50 latency <=10ms, your batch windows shrink so you lose some batching gains. also prefix/K V cache — pardon, K-V cash — can save a ton for repeated context. if many requests share prefixes (like standard system prompts) you get big wins.
[02:03] Priya: We have a lot of repeated system prompts and product templates, so KV caching seems promising. how does Redwood charge when cache hits occur?
[02:10] Maya: cache hits avoid the full forward pass in many cases, so the per-token billed compute is lower. Hosted billing still counts tokens but the effective compute cost is reduced; on dedicated we can represent that as fewer GPU cycles so your unit price goes down accordingly. we can share a worked example in the pricing sheet.
[02:25] Samir: ok show us the worked example, please.
[02:28] Omar: also quantization profiles matter. 4-bit quant gives you better throughput but sometimes small accuracy regressions. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization per workload; that directly changes tokens/sec and cost.
[02:40] Aisha: security question — if we go dedicated in our VPC, who holds keys? we need customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs.
[02:48] Maya: for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM and keys stay in your control. audit logs can be forwarded to SIEM. we have SOC2 and an enterprise package that includes enhanced logging and retention. we'll send the SOC2 cert and HSM integration guide.
[03:02] Connor: latency for private — is that generally higher since it's on our network? we want consistent P95 under 120ms.
[03:08] Omar: network overhead can add some ms but you eliminate public routing. P95 mostly depends on model size, sequence length, and GPU type. with proper provisioning and NVLink topology you can meet 120ms P95 for the model sizes you're describing. we'll validate in the pilot.
[03:25] Priya: for pilot scope, we want: (1) apples-to-apples hosted vs dedicated cost comparison, (2) cache hit rate estimates using our templates, and (3) latency profile under 2k concurrent sessions. is that doable?
[03:36] Omar: yes. propose Redwood runs a 48-hour benchmark: start with hosted runs to see baseline per-token burn and latencies, then spin up dedicated nodes (reserved) with same model and repeat. we'll instrument token-level costs, tokens/sec, batch sizes, prefix cache hit ratios, and tokenization breakdowns.
[03:51] Samir: timeline?
[03:53] Maya: we can get the pricing sheet and SOC2 links out by Monday. Omar can send a benchmark plan by next week. If we sync the pilot week of June 12th, that fits.
[04:03] Aisha: we also need a compliance questionnaire and standard DPA; please include in the package.
[04:08] Maya: yes we'll attach our DPA template and security questionnaire.
[04:11] Priya: costs — one more nit: how do you count tokens for streaming responses? we want to know per-response billing and also for function-calls where the model returns structured tokens.
[04:20] Omar: streaming counts tokens as they're generated; function-calls are tokenized same way. there's an edge case where smaller chunked streams increase overhead slightly but it's minor. We'll document examples from prior pilots.
[04:31] Connor: competitor question — can you run a side-by-side with Bedrock or Anthropic? we'd like to justify the migration cost.
[04:36] Maya: Redwood can run comparative cost/perf benchmarks, but we need explicit permission to spin up competitor tests on your cloud account; otherwise we can use public benchmarks. note that kernel-level optimizations and model variants differ.
[04:48] Priya: ok. success criteria for the pilot: average cost per 1k tokens under $Y (internal target, not quoted here), P95 latency <120ms, and K-V cache hit ratio >30% for templated flows.
[05:02] Omar: we will measure those and include a sensitivity analysis on batch window vs p50/p95 tradeoffs.
[05:08] Maya: any other blockers?
[05:11] Aisha: Data residency — if we run hosted in EU region is data encrypted at rest? yes? also we need evidence of penetration testing cadence.
[05:19] Maya: yes hosted EU region has encryption at rest and we can send pen test summaries and SOC2. for private we can meet any residency constraints since you're hosting in your VPC.
[05:29] Connor: one more - can we reserve burst capacity? some nights traffic spikes 3x.
[05:33] Omar: Dedicated can be configured with burst pools or autoscale policies; reserved capacity covers baseline, burst pays a smaller premium. we'll show cost model examples.
[05:43] Samir: great. price transparency is key for execs. if Redwood can present a model that shows total cost of ownership over 12 months vs Bedrock we can move quickly.
[05:54] Maya: we'll prepare a 12-month TCO slide in the follow-up.
[05:58] Priya: perfect, thanks.
[06:00] Maya: recap of next steps — send pricing, SOC2, DPA, security docs; Omar to send bench plan; schedule pilot week of June 12.
[06:10] Priya: thanks all. bye.

End of call.
